netcfg.bond.802.3ad: LACP (802.3ad) – needs a matching setting on the switch
netcfg.bond.balance-alb: Load balancing – without a setting on the switch
netcfg.vlanHint: 0 = no VLAN. Otherwise the NAS lives in the tagged network with this number.
netcfg.bridgeHint: This gives VMs an address of their own in the home network.
netcfg.needsPort: A fixed address, a VLAN or the bridge need at least one port to be chosen.
netcfg.trial: The change is on trial at first. Unless you confirm it within 2 minutes, the NAS goes back to the present setting by itself. If the address changes, open the web UI at the new address, log in and confirm there.
netcfg.pendingHere: A change is active on trial. Confirm it in the bar at the top, otherwise the NAS goes back to the previous setting.
netcfg.pending: New network setting on trial. Without confirmation it goes back to the previous one in {seconds} s.
settings.timezoneDesc: Applies to schedules and logs of the NAS and is handed to new apps.
vms.form.netBridge: An address of its own in the home network (bridge br0)
vms.form.netNoBridge: An address of its own needs the bridge. Set it up under
error.invalid_network: The network setting is not valid:
error.network_pending: A change is still on trial. Confirm or give it up first.
error.network_failed: The network setting could not be applied:
error.invalid_timezone: The NAS does not know this time zone.
error.no_bridge: The bridge br0 is not set up. Set it up under Settings › Network or switch the VM to “outgoing only”.
netcfg.lost: The NAS does not answer here right now – it probably has another address now. Open the web UI at the new address, log in and confirm the change there. Without confirmation the NAS is reachable at the previous address again after 2 minutes.
auth.codeHint: This account is protected with a second factor. Enter the six-digit code from your app – or one of your recovery codes.
account.title: My account
account.passwordText: The password is for the web UI and for your SMB shares.
account.twoFactorOff: Off. The password is enough to log in.
account.twoFactorOn: On. Logging in and confirming sensitive actions, such as opening VM consoles, also ask for a code from your authenticator app.
account.scan: Scan the code with an authenticator app (for example Aegis, 2FAS or your password manager) or enter the secret by hand.
account.enterCode: Code from the app, as a check
account.recoveryText: Each of these codes gets you in once without your phone. They are only shown now: keep them in a safe place, not on the NAS.
account.disableText: After that the password alone is enough again. Enter your password and a code to confirm.
account.devicesNote: Logins end after 7 days without use, after 30 days at the latest, and with every restart of the NAS.
error.second_factor_required: Please enter the code from your authenticator app.
error.invalid_code: The code is wrong or was used already.
error.two_factor_not_begun: The setup was not begun. Please start it again.
error.session_not_found: This login does not exist any more.
welcome.title: Welcome to TitanOS
welcome.intro: Your account exists. Two more things, then on to the storage.
welcome.hostnameHint: The NAS shows up in the network under this name. Lower-case letters, digits and hyphens.
welcome.timezoneHint: The time zone of this browser is suggested.
welcome.networkNow: The NAS is reachable at {address} right now. Your router hands out the address.
welcome.networkHint: A NAS should always be reachable at the same address. The easiest way is to reserve the address in the router; alternatively set a fixed one here.
welcome.networkSettings: Set up a fixed address, the bridge or a VLAN
welcome.doneText: The base system is ready. These steps make sense next:
welcome.todoVolumeText: Combine disks into a RAID. Without a volume nothing can be stored.
welcome.todoShareText: Folders reachable in the network over SMB or NFS.
welcome.todoTwoFactorText: Protects your account with a code from your phone as well.
welcome.todoAppsText: Switch Docker on and install apps from the store.
notify.title: Notifications
notify.empty: No notifications. This is where you see when a volume or a disk needs attention.
notify.sinceStart: Notifications since the NAS was last started.
notify.settingsDesc: E-mail and push messages for disk errors, rebuilds and full volumes.
notify.intro: TitanOS tells you when a volume loses a disk, is being rebuilt or is almost full, and when a disk reports errors or gets too warm. The notifications always show in the header; here you set where else they are sent.
notify.emailHint: Through the mailbox of a mail provider (SMTP). Many providers want an app password of its own for this.
notify.securityNone: Without encryption messages cross the network in the open, and a password is not sent. Only for a mail server in your own network.
notify.ntfyHint: Push to your phone through ntfy.sh or an ntfy server of your own. Whoever knows the name of the topic can read along – pick a long name that cannot be guessed.
notify.telegramHint: Create a bot with @BotFather, send it a message and enter its token and the number of your chat.
notify.discordHint: Create a webhook in the channel settings under Integrations and enter its address here.
notify.secretStored: stored – leave empty to keep it
notify.test: Save and send a test message
notify.testOk: Test message sent. Check whether it arrived.
notify.testFailed: The test message did not get through:
notify.kind.test.title: Test message
notify.kind.test.text: If you can read this, this way of notifying works.
notify.kind.volume_degraded.title: Volume {subject}: a disk is missing
notify.kind.volume_degraded.text: The volume goes on without redundancy. Replace the failed disk soon; if another one fails, the data is lost.
notify.kind.volume_failed.title: Volume {subject} has failed
notify.kind.volume_failed.text: The volume lacks too many disks. It cannot be used any more.
notify.kind.volume_rebuilding.title: Volume {subject}: rebuild in progress
notify.kind.volume_rebuilding.text: Until the rebuild is done the volume is not fully protected again.
notify.kind.volume_ok.title: Volume {subject} is in order again
notify.kind.volume_ok.text: The volume is complete and in sync.
notify.kind.volume_missing.title: Volume {subject} was not found
notify.kind.volume_missing.text: The disks of the volume are not there. Shares, apps and VMs on it stand still.
notify.kind.volume_mismatch.title: Volume {subject}: the check found differences
notify.kind.volume_mismatch.text: The check found blocks whose copies differ. Have a look at the volume under Storage.
notify.kind.volume_full.title: Volume {subject} is almost full
notify.kind.disk_unhealthy.title: Disk {subject} reports errors
notify.kind.disk_unhealthy.text: The self-diagnosis (SMART) reports an error. Back up the data and replace the disk.
notify.kind.disk_hot.title: Disk {subject} is very warm
notify.kind.disk_hot.text: The disk is warmer than 55 °C. Check the ventilation.
error.invalid_notify_settings: These entries do not fit. Check the marked fields.
error.notify_test_failed: The test message did not get through.

stick.title: Back up system configuration
stick.settingsDesc: Copies of the configuration on a volume – and how to replace a broken stick.
stick.intro: Everything that makes up your NAS – accounts, volumes, shares, apps, network – lives on the stick only, and sticks break. So TitanOS puts copies of the configuration on a volume: once after every start and after every change. With a copy you set up a new stick in a few minutes.
stick.off: The automatic backup is off. If the stick fails, you have to set up the NAS again by hand.
stick.noVolume: No volume is mounted. The backup starts by itself as soon as there is one.
stick.volumeMissing: The chosen volume {volume} is not mounted. Until it is, nothing is saved.
stick.ok: The configuration is saved. Newest copy from {time} on {volume}.
stick.ran: Checked. A new copy is only made when something changed.
stick.enabledHint: After every start and a few minutes after every change.
stick.downloadHint: Download a copy now and then and keep it away from the NAS. It holds password hashes and all secrets of your apps – treat it like a password.
stick.confirmReason: A backup holds password hashes and all secrets of the NAS. Enter your password once more to download it.
stick.replaceIntro: When the stick fails or you want to swap it as a precaution:
stick.step1: Download the zip of the same TitanOS version from the release page on GitHub.
stick.step2: Format a new stick with FAT32 and the name TITANOS and copy the content of the zip onto it.
stick.step3: Plug in the new stick and start the NAS. The disks stay as they are.
stick.step4: Open the web interface. Instead of creating a new account choose “Restore the configuration”: TitanOS finds the copies on the disks by itself. Then the NAS restarts and is its old self again.
stick.replaceNote: If the disks are gone as well, use a downloaded copy in the same step. After the restore the NAS is reachable at the address it had before.
restore.found: There is a backup on the disks
restore.foundText: This stick is new, but the disks of this NAS hold copies of a configuration. You can put one back instead of setting everything up again.
restore.fromFile: Restore a backup from a file
restore.fileHint: A copy you downloaded under “Backup of the stick” (titanos-config-….tar.gz).
restore.or: Or set up the NAS anew:
restore.confirmText: Accounts, volumes, shares, apps and network settings from the backup are written to this stick. Then the NAS restarts, and you log in with the account you had.
restore.confirmAddress: If the NAS had a fixed address, it is reachable at that one again after the restart – not necessarily at the current one.
restore.working: Writing the configuration to the stick …
restore.restarting: The configuration is back in place. The NAS is restarting …
restore.restartingHint: The page reloads by itself once the NAS is back. If it stays like this, the NAS probably has its former address again – open it there.
notify.kind.config_backup_failed.title: Backup of the stick failed
notify.kind.config_backup_failed.text: The configuration could not be saved to the volume {subject}. Have a look at Settings › Backup of the stick.
notify.kind.usb_plugged.title: USB drive {subject} plugged in
notify.kind.usb_plugged.text: Mount it under Files › Other drives to copy files.
error.backup_no_volume: No volume is mounted that could be saved to.
error.backup_not_found: This backup is not there any more.
error.not_a_backup: This is not a backup of a TitanOS configuration, or the file is damaged.
restore.slow: This takes longer than expected. The former certificate came back with the configuration – your browser may therefore ask once more whether to trust the page. Reload the page.
tools.bundleText: For a bug report on GitHub: a zip file with the logs and the state of the system. It is only made when you click and is not sent anywhere – you download it and decide yourself whom to give it to.
tools.bundleInText: Logs since the last start, kernel messages, disks and volumes, the state of the network, running services, containers (name, image, state), hardware and the settings of volumes, shares, network and VMs.
tools.bundleOutText: IP and hardware addresses, e-mail addresses, the name of the NAS, account names and whatever looks like a password, token or key are replaced. Accounts and password hashes, compose files and secrets of apps, certificates, notification settings and your files are never in it.
tools.bundleCheck: No filter is perfect. Look through the files before you attach the bundle in public – names of shares, containers and VMs are kept.
tools.bundleFailed: The diagnostic bundle could not be made.
tools.logsNote: The log is kept in memory and starts anew with every start of the NAS.
error.logs_failed: The log could not be read.
disktest.title: Preparing disks
disktest.intro: New disks are most likely to fail in their first days. So test them before they go into a volume: TitanOS reads or overwrites the whole disk and then lets it run its own long self-test (SMART).
disktest.none: There is no disk that could be tested. Only disks that are in no volume are tested.
disktest.mode.readHint: Reads the whole disk and starts the self-test. What is on the disk stays.
disktest.mode.writeHint: Writes a pattern to every place, reads it back and compares. More thorough – and everything on the disk is gone afterwards.
disktest.estimate: Rough estimate for {size}: about {hours} h. The disk's self-test is included and takes a different time depending on the model.
disktest.eraseWarning: All data on {disk} ({model}) will be erased for good.
disktest.eraseContents: There is something on the disk: {contents}.
disktest.restartNote: The test goes on in the background, even when you leave the page. A restart of the NAS ends it.
disktest.passedText: No errors found. The disk can go into a volume.
disktest.failedText: Do not put this disk into a volume. If it is new, return it.
disktest.note.io_errors: Places on the disk could not be written or read, or came back changed ({detail}).
disktest.note.smart_unsupported: The disk offers no self-test (a virtual disk or a USB adapter). This part was skipped.
disktest.note.smart_failed: The self-test of the disk failed: {detail}
disktest.note.smart_unhealthy: The disk reports itself as failing (SMART).
disktest.note.smart_counters: Defective or pending sectors were added during the test ({detail}).
disktest.note.smart_aborted: The self-test of the disk was stopped after four days.
notify.kind.disk_test_passed.title: Disk {subject} passed the test
notify.kind.disk_test_passed.text: The test ran through without errors. The disk can go into a volume.
notify.kind.disk_test_failed.title: Disk {subject} failed the test
notify.kind.disk_test_failed.text: The test found errors. Do not put the disk into a volume; details are under Tools.
error.disk_test_running: This disk is being tested already.
error.disk_test_not_found: There is no test of this disk.
ssh.onlyAdmins: Only owners and administrators log in over SSH. Keys you store here count once your account has one of these roles.
ssh.offHint: SSH access is switched off. Your keys count as soon as it is switched on.
ssh.onHint: With one of these keys you log in like this:
ssh.keyHint: The one line from the file ending in .pub (for example ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub). Never the private key.
access.title: Access
access.settingsDesc: SSH for administrators, the certificate of the web interface and API keys for agents.
access.sshText: For working on the command line from another computer. Only owners and administrators can log in, under their own name and with a key they stored under “My account” – never with a password and never as root. For commands with full rights there is sudo.
access.sshFingerprint: Fingerprint of the NAS (compare at the first login)
access.sshNoKeys: No owner or administrator has stored a key yet.
access.sshNote: Whoever has a key gets in without a password and without a second factor and has full rights with sudo. The system image is fresh at every start: only what lies under /config and /mnt stays.
access.certNone: In development mode the web interface runs without encryption.
access.certSelf: TitanOS made this certificate itself. The connection is encrypted, but the browser cannot check who is at the other end and warns for that reason. With a certificate of your own – say from the certificate authority of your home network or for a domain of yours – the warning goes away.
access.certExpiring: This certificate is only valid for {days} more days. Put a new one in place in time.
access.certSaved: The certificate is in place and in use from now on. Reload the page so that your browser uses it.
access.certOwn: Use a certificate of your own
access.certRemove: Remove and use the one from TitanOS again
access.certFormHint: Paste certificate and key in PEM format or choose the files.
access.certChain: Certificate, followed by the intermediate certificates
access.certKeyNote: The key is stored on the stick and never handed out again by the web interface.
notify.kind.certificate_expiring.title: The certificate is about to expire
notify.kind.certificate_expiring.text: The own certificate of the web interface is only valid until {subject}. Put a new one in place under Settings › Access.
error.invalid_ssh_key: This is not a public SSH key. Expected is one line like “ssh-ed25519 AAAA… name”, without options in front.
error.too_many_ssh_keys: An account cannot have more keys.
error.ssh_key_not_found: This key is not there any more.
error.invalid_key_name: The name may have at most 40 characters, may not start or end with a space and may not be on another key already.
error.invalid_scope: Choose at least one of the scopes offered.
error.invalid_key_network: A network is not valid. Examples: 192.168.1.0/24 or 192.168.1.20.
error.too_many_keys: An account cannot have more keys.
error.key_not_found: This key does not exist any more.
assistant.title: AI assistant
assistant.intro: Ask about your NAS or give it work: sort files, write documents, set up apps or change settings. Execution mode and allowed areas are configured in settings.
assistant.suggest.disks: Are my volumes and disks all right?
assistant.suggest.containers: Which containers are running, and are there updates?
assistant.suggest.backups: Are my backups up to date?
assistant.suggest.errors: Were there errors in the system log since the start?
assistant.note: Chats are kept on a volume of this NAS. Answers of a model can be wrong.
assistant.enable: Switch on the chat with the AI assistant
assistant.settingsText: A model from Ollama answers questions about this NAS in a chat and does work, with the rights of the account that is logged in. Changes it proposes as a card; for a job with several steps you approve the plan once. Open the chat with the speech bubble in the header, the round button at the bottom right or Ctrl+J.
assistant.ollamaHint: By default the Ollama app on this NAS. Another computer in the home network works too, such as http://192.168.1.20:11434.
assistant.modelHint: The model must be able to call tools, such as qwen3:8b or llama3.1:8b. Models without tools are not offered. Each account can pick another one in the chat.
assistant.privacy: The model gets your questions, attachments and the results of the tools: names of volumes, disks, shares, containers and VMs, usage, states, notifications and files it reads. Logs read through tools arrive redacted (addresses, account names, passwords); what you attach yourself does not. If Ollama runs on this NAS or in your home network, none of it leaves your network – except search terms and addresses of the web search, if it is on. The model never sees secrets such as backup passwords and .env files.
assistant.introUser: Ask about your shares and files or how something works. The assistant uses your account permissions and the configured execution mode.
assistant.noteMemory: No volume mounted: chats last only until the next restart. Answers of a model can be wrong.
assistant.memoryOnly: No volume is mounted. Chats are kept only until TitanOS restarts.
assistant.allowUsers: Users may use the assistant too
assistant.allowUsersText: In the chat, users see only their own shares and files and the manual – no disks, containers, VMs, logs or settings. For them, the assistant can only propose creating, renaming and deleting in shares they may write to.
assistant.webText: The assistant then searches the web for questions on software, hardware or error messages and reads single pages. Search terms go to DuckDuckGo, and pages are loaded by this NAS. Addresses on the home network, the tailnet and the NAS itself are blocked. The pages used are listed below the answer.
assistant.webUsers: Web search for users as well
assistant.actionsText: For each area choose no access, read access or changes. Execution mode determines whether the agent asks or acts directly. Secrets (passwords, backup passwords, .env, private keys) and consoles remain excluded.
assistant.volumeHint: Chats are kept per account in /mnt/<volume>/.titanos/assistant, readable by root only, never on the stick. Without a mounted volume they last until the next restart. Nobody sees the chats of another account.
assistant.promptPlaceholder: For example: Always answer in English. Our media is in the share Media.
assistant.promptHint: Additional instructions alongside the system prompt, up to 24,000 characters.
assistant.numCtxHint: 0 keeps what Ollama is set to.
assistant.temperatureHint: 0 to 2; empty keeps what the model says.
assistant.noToolsModel: no tools – not usable for the chat
assistant.pullHint: Find names at ollama.com/library. Large models need a lot of space and memory.
assistant.deleteModelText: {name} is deleted from Ollama. It can be loaded again later.
assistant.floating: Show the round chat button at the bottom right
assistant.unavailable: The AI assistant is not available
assistant.unavailableAdmin: Switch it on under Settings › AI assistant and pick a model from Ollama.
assistant.unavailableUser: It is off or not allowed for users. Ask an administrator.
assistant.noVision: This model cannot see images; it only learns the name of the file.
assistant.pageContext: Send the page I came from
assistant.pageContextHint: The assistant learns from which page you opened the chat, so that “this VM” or “here” is understood.
assistant.after: This proposal came after the assistant read content from outside ({tools}). Such content can contain instructions that are not yours – check it carefully.
assistant.confirmDanger: I know what this does and want it.
assistant.askLine: Ask the assistant about this line
assistant.askLog: Explain the errors and warnings in this part of the system log and what I can do.
assistant.askLogLine: What does this line in the system log mean, and do I need to do anything? “{line}”
assistant.askNotice: What does this notification ({time}) mean and what should I do? “{title}: {text}”
assistant.askBackup: The backup “{job}” failed. Why, and what can I do?
assistant.askAppSetup: Setting up the app “{app}” failed. Why, and what can I do?
assistant.askFile: Look at the file “{name}” and explain what it says.
assistant.askFileFailed: The file could not be given to the assistant.
assistant.suggest.howto: Write me a Word file with an overview of my volumes and disks into the first share.
assistant.suggest.shares: Which shares can I open and how much space is free?
assistant.suggest.files: Which files are in my first share?
assistant.action.app.update: Update app {name} (new image, container made anew)
assistant.action.app.purge: Delete app {name} with its data, Docker volumes and images
assistant.action.apps.updateAll: Update all apps with a new image: {apps}
assistant.action.vm.poweroff: Force off VM {name} (like pulling the plug)
assistant.action.vm.purge: Delete VM {name} with all its disks
assistant.action.volume.delete: Delete volume {name} with all its data
assistant.action.volume.create: Create volume {name} ({level}, {filesystem}) – everything on {disks} is erased
assistant.action.disk.testRead: Test disk {disk} ({model}) by reading – data stays
assistant.action.disk.testWrite: Overwrite and test disk {disk} ({model}) – everything on it is erased
assistant.action.share.delete: Remove share {name} – its files stay on the volume
assistant.action.update.rollback: Go back to the previous TitanOS version (the NAS restarts)
assistant.action.update.appRollback: Go back to the previous app version of titand
assistant.action.power.reboot: Restart the NAS – containers and VMs are stopped cleanly
assistant.action.power.poweroff: Shut down the NAS – containers and VMs are stopped cleanly
assistant.areasHint: Users (not administrators) only ever reach their own shares and files.
assistant.areaText.files: Read, search, write documents (Word, Excel, PDF, text), move, copy, rename, delete
assistant.areaText.docker: Containers, apps, compose files, app store
assistant.areaText.storage: Volumes, disks, checks, disk tests, sleep
assistant.areaText.backups: Backup jobs, restoring, backup of the stick
assistant.areaText.system: Network, SSH, notifications, UPS, energy, plugins, log, USB
assistant.areaText.updates: TitanOS updates, restarting or shutting down the NAS
assistant.maxStepsHint: How often the model may use tools for one answer. When the limit is reached or it repeats itself, it answers with what it found. “Unlimited” ends after 500 rounds at most.
assistant.autoRunning: Running as part of the task …
assistant.taskNote: An approved plan permits its non-destructive steps without more clicks. Direct mode also executes destructive steps without asking. Follow-up instructions steer the current job; Stop ends it.
assistant.attachNas: Attach a file from the NAS
assistant.nasText: Up to {count} files: text, Word, Excel or images. The NAS reads them itself, with the rights of your account.
assistant.action.file.replace: Replace {path} in {root} ({format}) – the old version stays as .prev
error.assistant_off: The AI assistant is switched off (Settings › AI assistant).
error.invalid_assistant: The Ollama address or the model name is not valid.
error.model_tool_parse: The model repeatedly generated an invalid tool call. Nothing from these responses was executed. Resume the task or choose another tool-capable model.
error.ollama_failed: Ollama is not reachable or reported an error.
error.assistant_no_model: No model is chosen. Pick one at the bottom of the chat or under Settings › AI assistant.
update.title: Updates
update.settingsDesc: New versions of TitanOS, the way back to the former one and the channel.
update.noKey: This image holds no key that updates could be verified with. Without a valid signature TitanOS installs nothing – for a development build that is the normal case. For a new version you write the stick anew.
update.downloading: Loading the new version onto the stick
update.failed: The update could not be installed. The running system is unchanged.
update.pendingUpdate: TitanOS {version} is on the stick and starts with the next restart.
update.pendingRollback: With the next restart TitanOS {version} starts again.
update.unconfirmed: This system is still on trial. In a few minutes it counts as confirmed; until then nothing else can be switched.
update.slots: The two systems on the stick
update.slotsText: The stick holds two systems. An update always goes into the one that is not running and starts three times on trial. If it does not come up, the NAS starts the former one again by itself.
update.slot.runningNotNext: running – the other one starts with the next restart
update.rollbackText: With the next restart the other system starts again. Your settings and data stay as they are.
update.rollbackWarn: An older version does not know settings that only the newer one introduced. They are not applied then.
update.betaHint: Beta versions are for trying out and may contain errors. Going back to the former version always stays possible.
update.autoHint: When TitanOS finds an update, it installs it at the chosen time. A system update then restarts the NAS, stopping containers and VMs. An app update restarts only the web interface and waits until no copies, backups or disk tests are running.
update.manualHint: TitanOS looks once a day and tells you when there is something new. It installs only when you say so.
update.confirmText: TitanOS loads {size} onto the stick, into the system that is not running. That takes a few minutes; the NAS keeps working meanwhile. The new version only becomes active with a restart that you trigger yourself.
update.confirmSafe: The signature of the release and the checksum of every file are verified. The current version stays as the fallback.
update.app.restarting: The web interface is restarting … Containers, VMs and shares keep running.
update.app.restarted: TitanOS {version} is running. The NAS was not restarted for it.
update.app.trial: The new version runs on trial. If it is not ready within a few minutes, TitanOS goes back to the previous one by itself.
update.app.title: App updates
update.app.text: Small updates replace only the TitanOS program with its web interface, not system image {version}. The NAS does not restart for them.
update.app.rollbackText: TitanOS restarts its web interface, which takes about half a minute. Containers, VMs and shares keep running; the NAS does not restart.
update.app.confirmText: TitanOS loads {size} onto the stick and then restarts only its web interface, which takes about half a minute. Containers, VMs and shares keep running; the NAS does not restart. While copies, backups or disk tests are running the update is refused; with “Install updates by themselves” it waits until they are done.
update.app.confirmSafe: The signature of the release and the checksum are verified. The new version first runs on trial; if it does not start, TitanOS goes back to the current one by itself.
notify.kind.update_available.title: TitanOS {subject} is available
notify.kind.update_available.text: A new version of TitanOS is out. You find it under Settings › Updates.
notify.kind.update_installed.title: TitanOS {subject} is running
notify.kind.update_installed.text: The update is installed and started. The former version stays on the stick as a fallback.
notify.kind.update_failed.title: Update to TitanOS {subject} failed
notify.kind.update_failed.text: The new version did not start. The NAS runs the former one again.
notify.kind.update_rolled_back.title: Back on TitanOS {subject}
notify.kind.update_rolled_back.text: The NAS runs this version again.
error.update_no_key: This image holds no key to verify updates with.
error.update_bad_signature: The release is not signed with a key this TitanOS trusts. It is not installed.
error.update_bad_manifest: The release is signed, but its description is unusable.
error.update_busy: An update is already running or waits for the restart.
error.update_too_old: This version cannot go to the new release directly:
error.update_no_space: There is not enough room on the stick for a second system:
error.update_unconfirmed: The running system is still on trial. Try again in a few minutes.
error.update_working: Copies, backups, disk tests or driver builds are running. An update without a restart would break them off; try again when they are done.
about.title: About TitanOS
about.settingsDesc: Version, license and the software TitanOS builds on.
about.licenseText: TitanOS is Fair Source. Its own code is under the Functional Source License (FSL-1.1-ALv2): you may use, read, change and pass it on – only not to make a competing commercial product or a competing service out of it.
about.licenseLater: Every version is put under the Apache License 2.0 two years after it came out. The date is on the page of each release.
about.thirdPartyText: The system image is a collection. The Linux kernel, the Debian packages and the libraries in use keep their own licenses; the sources of the GPL parts are linked with every release.
backup.title: Data backups
backup.settingsDesc: Copies of your shares on another volume, another server or in the cloud.
backup.intro: A RAID protects against the failure of a disk, not against deleting, ransomware, fire or theft. A backup copies your shares to another place at regular times – encrypted, so that nobody there can read along, and with the states of the last days, weeks and months.
backup.noShares: There is no share on a mounted volume that could be backed up.
backup.removeText: TitanOS forgets this job and its password. What was backed up already stays where it is and can still be read with restic and the password – write it down first if you still need the data.
backup.name: Name
backup.nameHint: Letters (A–Z, a–z), digits and hyphens. Cannot be changed later.
backup.onlyHint: Only the ticked folders are saved, with everything below them.
backup.allHint: Everything is saved. Untick folders that should be left out.
backup.noFolderChosen: Choose at least one folder of {share} or save the whole share.
backup.extra.configHint: The settings hold accounts, password hashes and 2FA secrets. The backup is encrypted; the job's password protects them.
backup.patterns: Leave out files (one pattern per line)
backup.patternsHint: For example *.tmp or node_modules. The recycle bin and half-finished uploads are always left out. Disks of running VMs are saved crash-consistent only.
backup.kindHint.titanos: A second NAS running TitanOS takes the backup, preferably over Tailscale. The backup is encrypted; the other NAS cannot read it.
backup.pairCodeHint: Make the code on the other NAS under Settings › Backups › “Accept backups of other TitanOS”.
backup.pairCodeInvalid: This is not a valid pairing code.
backup.targetDesc: This NAS can store the backups of other TitanOS. It is reached over Tailscale only, not in the home network and not on the internet.
backup.targetProblem.tailscale: Tailscale is not connected. Set it up under Plugins; without it this NAS accepts nothing.
backup.targetProblem.volume: The chosen volume is not mounted.
backup.targetPairHint: The name only appears here and names the folder. The code is shown once.
backup.targetCodeText: Paste this code into a backup job on the sending NAS under “Another TitanOS”.
backup.targetCodeOnce: The code holds the access and is not shown again. If it is lost, remove the NAS here and pair it again.
backup.targetRemoveText: The NAS can send nothing afterwards. Its stored backups stay unless you delete them on purpose.
backup.targetDeleteData: Also delete the stored backups of this NAS
backup.targetDeleteWarn: {size} will be deleted for good. Without this data and the job's password nothing can be restored.
backup.kindHint.local: A folder on another volume of this NAS. Protects against the failure of a volume and against deleting by mistake, not against fire or theft.
backup.kindHint.s3: Storage in the cloud that speaks the S3 protocol: Amazon S3, Backblaze B2, Wasabi, Hetzner Object Storage, a MinIO of your own and others.
backup.kindHint.sftp: Another machine that can be reached over SSH – a second NAS, a server or a storage box. The NAS logs in there with a key of its own.
backup.kindHint.rest: A server that runs the REST server of restic.
backup.publicKeyHint: Put this line into the file authorized_keys of the user on the server. At the first connection TitanOS remembers the server; if another one answers under the same name later, the backup stops.
backup.minute: Minute of the hour (the hour is ignored)
backup.window: Only start inside a time window
backup.windowHint: A backup that is due outside the window waits until the window opens. The window may pass midnight. A running backup is not cut short when the window ends.
backup.catchUp: If the NAS was off at the planned time, it catches up after the start. The first backup begins right after setting it up.
backup.keepHint: This many states stay: the newest of each of the last days, weeks and months. Older ones are removed after every backup. 0 everywhere keeps all.
backup.warning: The backup was made, but not everything could be read:
backup.passwordReason: With this password the backup can be read. Enter your own password once more to see it.
backup.passwordText: The backup is encrypted with this password. TitanOS knows it; but if the NAS itself is lost, you need it to get at your data.
backup.passwordWarn: Write it down now or put it into your password manager – apart from the NAS. Without the password the backup is worthless, and nobody can reset it.
backup.restoreLoading: Reading the states that are there …
backup.restoreNone: There is no state yet that something could be restored from.
backup.restoreText: The chosen state is copied into a new folder. What lies in your shares now is not touched – you take from there what you need.
backup.restoreStarted: The restore is running. The files end up here:
backup.restoreWhere: You find the folder under Files › Volumes. The progress shows on this page.
notify.kind.backup_failed.title: Backup {subject} failed
notify.kind.backup_failed.text: The backup did not run through. Details are under Settings › Backups.
notify.kind.backup_overdue.title: Backup {subject} has not worked for a while
notify.kind.backup_overdue.text: No backup has worked for at least two runs and two days. Check under Settings › Backups whether the target can be reached.

error.backup_job_not_found: This backup is not there any more.
error.backup_job_running: This backup is at work right now.
error.backup_no_sources: None of the shares of this backup is available right now.
error.usb_not_found: This drive is no longer connected.
error.usb_unsupported: The filesystem of this drive cannot be mounted.
error.usb_busy: The drive is still in use. Close open files and try again.
error.folder_unreadable: This folder of the share cannot be read.
error.invalid_backup_target: The input does not fit (name: letters (A–Z, a–z), digits and -; the volume must be mounted).
error.backup_source_exists: A NAS with this name is paired already.
error.backup_target_no_tailscale: Tailscale is not connected, so there is no address for the code yet.

ups.title: UPS
ups.settingsDesc: Uninterruptible power supply: shut down cleanly in a power failure.
ups.intro: A UPS bridges a power failure with its battery. TitanOS reads its state through NUT (Network UPS Tools) and shuts the NAS down cleanly before the battery is empty – with VMs and containers stopped and volumes unmounted, so that no RAID has to sync again.
ups.shuttingDown: The NAS is shutting down because of the power failure.
ups.modeHint.off: Without a UPS a power failure switches the NAS off hard.
ups.modeHint.local: The UPS is attached to this NAS by USB or serial cable. Most USB devices work with the driver usbhid-ups.
ups.modeHint.network: Another device (a second NAS, a server) has the UPS on its cable and passes its state on through NUT. This NAS listens and shuts down when that one says so.
ups.scan: Look for a UPS on USB
ups.serve: Tell other devices in the network the state of the UPS
ups.serveHint: With these details you set up NUT on other devices that are powered by the same UPS. They shut down first, then this NAS.
ups.serveAfterSave: After saving, the login for the other devices shows here.
ups.name: Name of the UPS there
ups.whenLow: When the UPS reports that the battery is almost empty
ups.whenHint: Shutting down earlier spares the battery and leaves a reserve for a second time. If the power comes back before, everything keeps running.
notify.kind.ups_on_battery.title: Power failure: the NAS runs on battery
notify.kind.ups_on_battery.text: The UPS powers the NAS. If the power does not come back, the NAS shuts down in time.
notify.kind.ups_online.title: The power is back
notify.kind.ups_online.text: The UPS is on mains power again.
notify.kind.ups_low_battery.title: Battery of the UPS almost empty
notify.kind.ups_low_battery.text: The UPS reports an almost empty battery. The NAS shuts down now.
notify.kind.ups_shutdown.title: The NAS is shutting down
notify.kind.ups_shutdown.text: The NAS ran {subject} minutes on battery and shuts down now, as set.
notify.kind.ups_lost.title: No connection to the UPS
notify.kind.ups_lost.text: The UPS does not answer any more. In a power failure the NAS cannot shut down in time like this.
storage.sleepHint: One idle timeout for all HDDs. Each disk sleeps after its own period without reads or writes and wakes on the next access.
storage.sleepDetails: SSDs, NVMe, the boot stick and disks passed through to VMs are excluded. Disk tests and RAID checks/rebuilds pause the timer. Apps and shares may keep disks awake. The first access after sleep can take a few seconds. Off disables automatic sleep by TitanOS; sleeping disks wake on their next access.
storage.sleepUnavailable: The setting could not be read from the boot stick. Automatic disk sleep remains disabled.
storage.sleepFailed: Sleep could not be enabled for the following disks. Some drives or USB enclosures do not support the command.
error.invalid_disk_idle_time: Please select one of the available idle timeouts.
accelerator.igpuHint: Integrated and discrete Intel and AMD graphics.
accelerator.nvidiaHint: An NVIDIA graphics card requires the matching NVIDIA plugin.
accelerator.unavailable: – = measurement unavailable from the driver. Updated every 5 seconds.
plugins.activationFailed: The plugin could not start. Check the hardware and service log under Tools, then retry activation.
plugins.integrityFailed: The installed plugin image does not match its checksum. Remove it and reinstall the original release files.
plugins.busy: The driver is still in use. Stop its containers and other GPU jobs before disabling the plugin.
error.plugin_downloading: This plugin is already being downloaded.
error.plugin_busy: The plugin is still in use. Stop its containers and GPU jobs first.
fs.btrfsDesc: Native mirror with checksums and snapshots.
snapshot.title: Snapshots
snapshot.mirrorOnly: Btrfs requires RAID 1 and exactly two disks.
snapshot.name: Snapshot name
snapshot.note: Snapshots share space with the volume and do not replace backups. Nested subvolumes (such as Docker) are excluded. Shut down running databases and VMs cleanly first.
snapshot.restoreNote: Restored data appears under {path}. Existing folders are never overwritten.
hardware.containerHint: Select an Intel/AMD GPU, NPU or NVIDIA GPU. Selections persist across reboots; devices used by a running VM are blocked. The app needs compatible libraries inside its container.
hardware.autoGPU: Automatically switch NVIDIA between this VM and containers
hardware.autoGPUHint: Starting the VM stops containers using its NVIDIA GPU. Once the VM exits and the driver has reclaimed the GPU, TitanOS restarts exactly those containers. Without this option, running GPU containers block VM startup.
hardware.coralUSBWarning: Gives the app access to the whole USB device bus; use only with trusted apps. The app must include an Edge TPU runtime.
error.hardware_settings: This GPU does not support that power limit or it could not be applied.
plugins.catalogIntro: Install official plugins directly from GitHub. Only selected packages are downloaded, then stored on a data volume.
plugins.updateAvailable: Version {version} is ready in a share.
plugins.updateText: TitanOS checks the new version, stops the plugin briefly and starts it with the new version. If it does not start, the previous version comes back. A plugin that is in use stays as it is.
plugins.catalogDevelopment: This development build does not belong to a published release. Official downloads require a released TitanOS version. You can still use plugins from shares.
plugins.catalogUnavailable: The plugin catalog for TitanOS {version} has not been published in full yet. Try again later or upload matching plugin files into a share.
plugins.catalogError: The GitHub catalog could not be downloaded or verified. Installed, local and previously verified plugins remain visible. Refresh the catalog to try again.
plugins.downloadNote: Download: {size}. TitanOS checks the signature, system version, kernel and checksum before activation. This may take a few minutes.
plugins.needVolume: A data volume must be mounted before installing.
error.plugin_download_failed: The plugin could not be downloaded. Check the internet connection and try again.
error.plugin_release_unavailable: No matching plugin download has been published for this TitanOS version yet.
energy.title: Energy
energy.intro: Choose from profiles reported by this NAS’s kernel and firmware. Saved profiles apply immediately and are restored at startup.
energy.governorHint: Controls how the processor adjusts frequency to demand. The meaning of “powersave” depends on the CPU driver.
energy.preferenceHint: Balances energy use and performance. Some drivers only allow the “performance” preference with the “performance” governor.
energy.platformHint: The manufacturer’s profile may adjust performance, cooling and energy use together.
energy.unsupported: This NAS exposes no adjustable energy profiles. This can happen in a VM or with limited firmware support.
energy.startupError: The saved profile could not be applied at startup.
energy.readOnly: Energy profiles are read-only in development mode.
error.energy_failed: The energy profile could not be applied.
dashboard.workloadMissing: “{name}” no longer exists or is currently unavailable.
dashboard.workloadAdmin: VM and container metrics require administrator access.
dashboard.vmCPUHint: CPU as a percentage of assigned vCPUs. RAM is memory occupied by the VM process.
dashboard.containerCPUHint: 100% CPU represents one fully used core.
vms.form.explicitDevices: Only selected devices are passed through. Select additional card functions explicitly.
vms.form.requiredCompanions: Functions {list} belong to the same card. Select the functions explicitly; functions sharing an isolation group must be selected together.
error.hardware_incomplete_group: Select the listed functions in the same IOMMU group. Nothing is added automatically.
error.hardware_in_use: A program on the NAS is still using the graphics device, for example a container with /dev/dri. Stop it and start the VM again; the log names the program. The device is not taken away from it while running, because that can bring the whole NAS down.
error.vm_hardware_busy: A Docker app is being started on this hardware, or a running app backup will restart a container that uses it. Try again afterwards.
error.plugin_update_pending: A system update is running or awaiting a restart. Complete or cancel it before changing plugins.
plugins.activateLaterHint: Without this option, the plugin is only installed on the data volume. Running VMs and containers remain unchanged. You can activate it later when the required hardware is available.
plugins.driverHint: New public NVIDIA versions are verified and downloaded to the data volume. You start compilation and then choose the driver for the next NAS reboot.
plugins.driverAutomatic: Check daily and download new source packages automatically
plugins.driverCheck: Check for a new NVIDIA version
plugins.driverPending: Selected for the next NAS reboot: {version}. Other plugin changes are blocked until reboot or cancellation.
plugins.driverState.unavailable: No matching build environment is available for this TitanOS version yet
plugins.driverState.error: Check failed; existing driver is retained
error.plugin_driver_pending: A driver change awaits reboot. Reboot the NAS or cancel the selection in the NVIDIA plugin before changing plugins.
temperatures.title: Temperatures
temperatures.description: Choose the temperature sensors you want to see on the dashboard.
temperatures.perAccount: This selection applies to your account. You can move and resize the tile on the dashboard.
temperatures.choose: Select at least one sensor under Settings → Temperatures.
temperatures.none: The kernel currently reports no supported temperature sensors.
temperatures.unavailable: – = Sensor is missing, suspended or not reporting a valid reading.
temperatures.missing: Currently not detected – selection is retained.
temperatures.sensorHint: Names come from the sensor driver. Unlabelled inputs are not assumed to be CPU or motherboard sensors. Drive temperatures are shown under Storage.
error.invalid_vm_display_name: The display name must be 1–80 characters long and must not contain control characters.
vms.displayNameInvalid: The display name must be 1–80 characters long and must not contain control characters.
create.firstFolders: The vms, appdata and iso folders are created automatically on the first volume.
dashboard.hostRAM: Resident host RAM of the QEMU process (RSS), not its allocation or application usage inside the guest.
dashboard.containerRAM: Container memory reported by the Docker daemon.
powerButton.title: Power button
powerButton.intro: Choose what a short press of the server’s power button does.
powerButton.shutdownHint: Restart and shutdown use the normal system sequence to stop services and VMs cleanly. Pressing the button does not show an additional confirmation dialog.
powerButton.longPress: Holding the button can force a hardware power-off. This setting does not change that.
error.power_button_failed: Could not apply the power button setting.
tailscale.activateHint: Enable the plugin to configure Tailscale.
tailscale.logout: Sign the NAS out of Tailscale
tailscale.logoutHint: The NAS will disconnect and require a new sign-in. Remote access through Tailscale will end.
tailscale.routesHint: One network prefix per line. Leave empty to expose only this NAS.
tailscale.exitNone: Do not use or advertise an exit node
tailscale.exitProvide: Offer this NAS as an exit node
tailscale.lanAccess: Direct local network access stays enabled.
tailscale.acceptRoutes: Accept subnet routes from other Tailscale devices
tailscale.approvalHint: Approve advertised subnets and this exit node in the Tailscale admin console. Your tailnet access rules determine who can connect.
tailscale.trial: Check access and confirm by {time}. Without confirmation, the previous settings will be restored.
tailscale.firewallHint: Tailscale manages IPv4/IPv6 rules for the encrypted tunnel, UDP port 41641 and forwarding. Subnet routing uses source NAT. These rules stay ahead of the general firewall allow rule. Tailscale SSH and automatic program updates are disabled.
tailscale.onlineOnly: Show only devices that are online
tailscale.device.inactive: The Tailscale plugin is not active.
tailscale.device.unknown: The state of Tailscale is unknown.
tailscale.device.noneVisible: None of the chosen devices are visible.
error.tailscale_failed: Tailscale could not complete the action.
netbird.activateHint: Enable the plugin to set up NetBird.
netbird.logout: Remove NAS from the NetBird network
netbird.logoutHint: The NAS deregisters from the management server and is deleted there as a peer. Remote access through NetBird ends; a new registration needs a setup key again.
netbird.keyNeeded: For its first login the NAS needs a setup key from the NetBird dashboard.
netbird.keyHint: The key is only used to register with the management server, stored on the stick and never shown again. An empty field keeps the stored key.
netbird.managementHint: Leave empty for NetBird Cloud. For a self-hosted server enter its address with port, e.g. https://netbird.example.org:443. Another server needs a setup key from there.
netbird.acceptRoutes: Accept routes from other NetBird peers
netbird.serveRoutes: Allow this NAS as routing peer or exit node
netbird.acceptDNS: Use the DNS settings of the NetBird network
netbird.policyHint: Networks, exit nodes and who may access what are set in the NetBird dashboard. Access to the local network always stays available.
netbird.trial: Please check access and confirm by {time}. Without confirmation the previous settings are restored.
netbird.firewallHint: NetBird manages its own nftables tables for the wt0 interface, UDP port 51820 and forwarding; its access rules apply regardless of the general firewall opening. Next to Tailscale, wt0 is accepted before Tailscale's rules because both use the 100.64.0.0/10 range. NetBird SSH, remote jobs and self-updates are off.
netbird.peer.inactive: The NetBird plugin is not active.
netbird.peer.unknown: The state of NetBird is unknown.
netbird.peer.none: No peers in the NetBird network.
netbird.peer.noneVisible: None of the chosen peers are visible.
error.netbird_failed: NetBird could not complete the action.
error.netbird_setup_key: This login needs a setup key.
plugins.driverBuildHint: The matching build environment and all working files stay on the plugin volume. At least 5 GiB free space is required; the build uses at most two CPU cores and 2 GiB RAM. Running GPU VMs and containers keep their current driver.
plugins.driverSource: NVIDIA {driver} · Container Toolkit {toolkit} · Source packages downloaded
plugins.driverState.sourceReady: Sources ready – you can start the build
plugins.driverState.building: Compiling the driver on this NAS
memoryPolicy.title: Memory
memoryPolicy.intro: Linux uses idle RAM as file cache and reclaims it when needed. This setting controls the write buffer budget for file transfers. Default: 20% of available RAM after the system reserve.
memoryPolicy.percent: Write buffer budget for file transfers
memoryPolicy.hint: The budget follows available RAM after a system reserve. Browser uploads are saved and released from cache in sections; adjusted kernel thresholds trigger earlier SMB/NFS writeback. This is not a fixed percentage limit for read cache, VM memory or the system image.
error.memory_policy_failed: The memory budget could not be applied.
error.upload_memory_pressure: Upload is waiting for available RAM.
error.upload_volume_unavailable: The target volume is no longer available. The upload has stopped.
vms.directoryHint: Optional folder name for new disks and firmware. Spaces are allowed; existing images are not moved.
vms.reuseDirectory: Also use image folder “{name}” for firmware
vms.lowSpace: Low space on {volumes}. Growing VM images may fill the volume and cause write errors in the guest.
vms.ov.cpuHistory: CPU load over the last two minutes
vms.ov.cdLive: Changes at once, like a disc. If the VM was already running before the last TitanOS update, only after its next start.
vms.ov.bridge: Own address in the home network (br0)
vms.ov.fromArp: seen by the NAS on the network
vms.ov.noAddress: None known yet. With the QEMU guest agent in the VM (package qemu-guest-agent) it shows up reliably.
vms.ov.noAddressUser: No address of its own on the network. With the QEMU guest agent in the VM its internal address shows up here.
vms.ov.gpuScreen: With a passed-through graphics card the picture appears on the card's monitor, not under “Screen”.
vms.ov.cdText: The medium is inserted when the VM starts next.
vms.ov.cdTextLive: The VM is running: the medium is inserted at once and replaces any disc in the drive.
vms.ov.cdSearching: Looking for ISO files on the volumes …
vms.ov.cdNone: There is no ISO file on the mounted volumes. Upload one to a share in the file manager.
uploads.recoverHint: Reselect the original file to resume. Previously received data is compared before continuing.
uploads.verifying: Comparing received data with the selected file…
create.changedDisks: The selected disks changed or are no longer available. Please select them again.
snapshots.title: Snapshots
snapshots.name: Snapshot name
snapshots.scope: Saves every virtual disk, VM configuration, UEFI and TPM on the VM volume. Snapshots on the same NAS do not replace an external backup.
snapshots.stopFirst: Shut down the VM cleanly before restoring.
snapshots.includeMemory: Include RAM state when the VM is running
snapshots.pauseInfo: The VM is unavailable during capture and then resumes from its saved RAM state. Large disks can take longer without fast filesystem copies. Network connections may time out.
snapshots.allowPause: I allow the interruption during capture.
snapshots.stoppedInfo: The VM is off. A snapshot without RAM state will be created.
snapshots.retention: Old scheduled snapshots are deleted only after a new capture succeeds. Manual snapshots are retained. Missed runs are skipped. Running VMs are skipped when RAM capture is disabled.
snapshots.restoreWarning: “{vm}” will return to “{name}”. Changes to virtual disks, VM configuration and firmware since this snapshot will be lost.
snapshots.restoreMemory: Resume saved RAM state and start the VM
snapshots.runtime: RAM restore requires the same QEMU version, firmware and host CPU. After relevant system changes, restore without RAM and boot the VM instead.
snapshots.deleteWarning: Permanently delete snapshot “{name}”? Current VM disks are retained.
snapshots.interrupted: A snapshot operation was interrupted. Starting, editing and additional snapshots are blocked until recovery.
snapshots.recoverInfo: An incomplete restore rolls back to the previous disks. An interrupted capture resumes saved RAM only when safe. If resume already began, TitanOS prevents replaying the same RAM state.
snapshots.discardMemory: Discard RAM state if needed; cold-start the VM afterwards. Unsaved work may be lost.
snapshots.job.running: Snapshot operation in progress. You can close this page.
snapshots.reason.passthrough: Snapshots are unavailable because this VM has PCI/USB passthrough devices.
snapshots.reason.folders: Complete snapshots are unavailable with shared NAS folders (virtiofs).
snapshots.reason.block: VM snapshots cannot capture physical disks passed directly to the guest.
snapshots.reason.disks: This VM has no virtual disk.
snapshots.reason.preparing: VM disks are still being prepared.
snapshots.reason.volume: A required volume is not mounted.
error.vm_snapshot_busy: An operation is already running for this VM. Wait for it to finish.
error.vm_snapshot_unsupported: This VM cannot be fully captured with its assigned devices or NAS folders.
error.vm_snapshot_recovery: Interrupted snapshot operation: recover it under Manage snapshots. If resume already began, explicitly discard RAM to allow a cold boot.
error.vm_snapshot_runtime: QEMU, firmware or CPU have changed. Restore without RAM state.
error.vm_snapshot_exists: Explicitly delete the VM snapshots before removing this VM.
error.vm_file_protected: This path belongs to a VM. Manage disks and firmware through VM settings; review its snapshots before removal.
snapshots.reason.iso: Eject the installation medium before taking a snapshot (Overview › Disks). The external ISO file is not captured.
editor.publicUrlHint: Full HTTP/HTTPS address, for example your Cloudflare tunnel. Does not create a tunnel. Leave empty to hide the button.
editor.publicUrlInvalid: Enter a full HTTP/HTTPS address without a username or password.
backup.kindHint.usb-copy: Directly readable, unencrypted copy. Changed files are replaced; deleted source files are retained. No version history. The selected drive is mounted when needed and left mounted afterwards. Links and special files are not copied and reported as errors.
backup.copyRestore: Copy files back using the file manager.
backup.copyPatterns: File or folder names, e.g. *.tmp. No paths or **.
sound.title: Notification sounds
sound.hint: For your account. Sounds play in the open browser after a click or keypress. Rapid notifications are grouped.
sound.blocked: The browser blocked playback. Check sound permissions and test again.
stick.schedule.hint: Startup and change-triggered backups remain active. The schedule checks the configuration; unchanged data does not create duplicate backups.
vms.form.firmwareNote: UEFI for modern systems; legacy BIOS for older systems or existing BIOS images. This choice is fixed when creating the VM.
vms.form.firmwareFixed: Boot firmware was fixed when this VM was created. It must match the installation on its virtual disk.
vms.form.biosWindows: Choose UEFI with TPM and Secure Boot for Windows 11. Legacy BIOS is intended for older Windows versions.
files.editHint: UTF-8 text files up to 512 KiB. The previous version is kept beside the file as .prev. Save with Ctrl+S or ⌘S.
files.editTooLarge: The text exceeds 512 KiB and cannot be saved here.
error.text_conflict: The file has changed since you opened it. Your draft is preserved. Reopen the current file and reconcile the changes.
error.not_text: This is not a supported UTF-8 text file, or it exceeds 512 KiB.
error.invalid_json: The content is not valid JSON. Check brackets, quotes and commas.
error.file_name_too_long: A file or folder name, or the path, is too long for the target filesystem. Shorten it; non-ASCII characters can occupy multiple bytes.
backup.kindHint.smb-copy: Copies selected folder trees to a second NAS. New and changed files are transferred; files deleted at the source remain at the destination. No version history: changed files replace the previous copy.
backup.smb.title: Second NAS as SMB backup destination
backup.smb.intro: Optional Beta feature for directly readable folder copies. Connect the destination first, then create a job with the source folders you want.
backup.smb.setup: First create a user and a writable SMB share on the second TitanOS/NAS. Enter its address and credentials here and discover shares. SMB3 encryption is required.
backup.smb.name: Destination name
backup.smb.keepPassword: Leave blank to keep the stored password
backup.smb.credentialsHint: The password is stored in the protected system configuration and is never shown again. The write test creates and removes a temporary file. Destination folders are created as needed.
backup.smb.save: Test write access and save destination
backup.smb.removeHint: Only the connection is removed. Previously copied files remain. Remove or change jobs that use this destination first.
backup.smb.noShares: No suitable shares found. Check the SMB user on the second NAS.
backup.smb.first: If no destination is available, close this dialog and configure an SMB destination above first. Files are stored under the job folder, share name and full relative source path.
update.singleChannel: All TitanOS updates use one stable channel. Individual new features are marked Beta in the interface.
files.chooseRoot: No data volume available. Choose a location from the list.
files.windowsLoadFailed: Could not load shares. Please open this dialog again.
files.windowsUnavailable: Open an existing SMB share folder. USB devices, the system stick and names containing invalid Windows characters cannot be mapped here.
files.windowsMapHint: Choose an unused drive letter. Copy the command into PowerShell on your Windows PC. The drive points directly to this folder, shortening the visible destination path. Windows uses your SMB login.
files.windowsCopyHint: For long folder trees: enter the local source folder and run the generated command in PowerShell. Robocopy copies all contents including subfolders. Changed destination files may be overwritten; extra destination files are retained.
files.windowsSource: Full source folder on your Windows PC
files.windowsLimits: This does not shorten subfolders within your source. Robocopy supports long paths; individual filename limits still apply. TitanOS does not change names or share permissions.
docker.layout.hint: Drag a handle or use the arrows to change the order. Saved for your account.
ui.stale: Displayed values may be out of date. Last updated {seconds} seconds ago.
ui.neverConnected: No current system data received yet.
ui.vmAccepted: Action for {name} accepted. The state will update automatically.
ui.backupAccepted: Request for {name} accepted. Progress will update automatically.

ha.title: Home Assistant
ha.intro: Connects TitanOS to your Home Assistant: the AI assistant can read and switch released devices, and notifications can go to your phone through the Home Assistant app.
ha.tokenHint: Create one in Home Assistant under Profile › Security › “Long-lived access tokens”. The token stays on the NAS and is never shown again. TitanOS only connects to exactly this address and does not follow redirects.
ha.fingerprintHint: Only needed when Home Assistant uses HTTPS with a self-signed certificate. Then exactly this certificate is accepted, no other.
ha.releaseIntro: The assistant only sees and switches what is released here: whole domains such as all lights, or single devices. Locks, covers, alarm panels and similar devices are switched only after a ticked confirmation. The area “Home Assistant” must also be switched on in the assistant's settings.
notify.haHint: Sends messages through a notify service of Home Assistant, for example to the app on your phone. Set up the connection under Settings › Home Assistant.

assistant.areaText.home: Read and switch released devices of Home Assistant (Settings › Home Assistant). Off by default.
automation.haHelp: Starts when the device's state changes, for example a person switching to “not_home” or a power meter rising above a value. Only devices released under Settings › Home Assistant can be chosen. Changes while the connection is down are not caught up.
notify.kind.ha_power_refused.title: Home Assistant: power action refused
notify.kind.ha_power_refused.text: Home Assistant asked the NAS to {subject}. TitanOS refused because copies, backups, disk tests or a volume rebuild are running.
ha.accountIntro: Buttons and switches in Home Assistant act for this account, with its rights, and every press is logged. Without an account TitanOS creates no buttons. TitanOS watches automations with Home Assistant triggers while the connection is up.
ha.watching: Connected: state changes for automations are being watched.
ha.watchError: The connection for automations is down; TitanOS keeps trying:

ha.commandGroups: Buttons and switches in Home Assistant
ha.command.power: Restart and shut down the NAS
ha.commandsWarning: Anyone allowed to write to your MQTT broker can press these buttons. Protect the broker with users and access rules. TitanOS refuses to restart or shut down while copies, backups, disk tests or a volume rebuild are running.
ha.commandsNoAccount: Choose an account above; without one TitanOS creates no buttons.
ha.mqttConnected: Connected to the broker; values are sent every 30 seconds.

agent.pushApprovalHint: Messages about waiting actions then carry the buttons “Approve” and “Reject” (ntfy and the Home Assistant app). Destroying actions are never approved from a message.
ha.assistHint: With the blueprint for Home Assistant you ask by voice or text “Ask the NAS …”. TitanOS answers as the chosen account; changes still need approval as in the AI assistant. The token must belong to an administrator in Home Assistant.

automation.tpl.containerUpdates.name: Report container updates
automation.tpl.containerUpdates.prompt: Check whether updates are available for Docker containers. If so, send me a short list with notify_me. If a check fails, say so explicitly. Do not install anything.
automation.tpl.backupFailed.name: Explain a failed backup
automation.tpl.backupFailed.prompt: A backup failed. Read the notifications, the state of the backup jobs and the log, explain the likely cause in two or three sentences and send it to me with notify_me. Do not change anything.
automation.tpl.usbPhotos.name: Sort photos from a USB drive
automation.tpl.usbPhotos.prompt: A USB drive was plugged in. Copy new photos and videos from it into the share “Photos”, in folders by year and month. Skip files that are already there. Do not delete or change anything on the USB drive. At the end, send me how many files were copied with notify_me. Choose the drive below and adjust the share name.
automation.tpl.volumeFull.name: Volume is filling up
automation.tpl.volumeFull.prompt: The volume is more than 85 % full. Find the largest folders and files and send me three concrete suggestions for cleaning up with notify_me. Do not delete anything. Choose the volume below.
automation.tpl.nobodyHome.name: Nobody at home
automation.tpl.nobodyHome.prompt: Nobody is at home any more. Check which containers and VMs are running and use much CPU or RAM, and send me a short summary with notify_me. Do not stop anything. Choose the person or group from Home Assistant below.

powerSchedule.rtcHint: Switching on uses the wake alarm of the mainboard (RTC). Some mainboards need a BIOS setting for it; this is not checked on this hardware.
powerSchedule.noRtc: This mainboard has no wake alarm (RTC); switching on by schedule is not possible here. Wake-on-LAN, for example from Home Assistant, is an alternative.
powerSchedule.wolHint: Use the MAC address to wake the NAS, for example in Home Assistant's Wake-on-LAN integration. Some mainboards also need a BIOS setting.

ops.window: Catch up in the next maintenance window
ops.pruneConsent: Delete older automatic snapshots of this schedule. Keep manual snapshots.

ops.reviewHint: The previous outcome is unknown. Inspect the target before allowing another run. Reviewing does not immediately start the job.
ops.unsavedHint: This draft has not been saved.
ops.monitorHint: Optional minute samples on a data volume. This can wake sleeping data disks. Interruptions appear as gaps. Disk latency is the mean of completed I/O operations.
ops.noSamples: No samples in the selected range.
ops.importHint: Supports assembled mdadm arrays with ext4/XFS and native two-device Btrfs mirrors. Preview mounts read-only without journal replay. Registration does not import accounts or shares.
ops.importReady: Read-only preview succeeded. Registration mounts the volume normally with write access.
ops.usageHint: On-demand scan, limited to 30 seconds and 200,000 entries. Logical sizes and allocated blocks do not add up to reclaimable space with hardlinks, reflinks and snapshots. Private operational data is excluded.
ops.incomplete: Incomplete scan — values are partial results.
ops.growHint: Adds one disk to healthy RAID 5/6 with ext4 or XFS. The new disk is erased. The recovery file and journal require a healthy separate volume on other physical disks. Other storage changes are blocked during the operation.
ops.eraseConsent: Erase all data on the selected new disk. A current external backup is available.
ops.growthPending: An expansion is pending. Keep the recovery volume connected and inspect the displayed state.
ops.snapshotHint: Select regular files only, up to 200 files and 10 GiB in total. Restore creates a new folder. Internal data and symlinks are excluded.
ops.cloneHint: The source VM must be stopped. Independent disks, firmware and TPM are copied. The clone gets a new UUID/MAC and no autostart. Passthrough devices, host folders, block disks and backing chains are unsupported.
ops.appHint: Cleanly stop selected applications for this backup or export PostgreSQL with pg_dumpall. Stopping requires explicit consent. Other running containers writing the same data block a cold copy.
ops.allowStop: Stop selected running containers and VMs for the backup.
ops.restartPrevious: Restart only the original instances that were running before.
ops.probeHint: Restores a bounded selection of regular files from the latest backup into a private test directory and verifies against the same snapshot. The test directory is removed afterwards.
ops.transferBlocked: Unknown file outcome — inspect source and destination before a new transfer.
ops.forgetHint: Removes only the saved record. Already copied files and remaining partial copies are unchanged.
ops.allClear: No pending errors in the loaded task states.
ops.stale: Refresh failed. The last known state remains visible.
ops.failed: The operation could not be completed.
ops.cancelGrowthHint: Cancels only an expansion that has not started and removes its new spare if present. Erased data on the new disk is not restored.

dashboard.visual.durationHint: CPU, threads, RAM, GPU and progress bars.

memoryPolicy.pressure: Time stalled on memory (some / all tasks)

memoryPolicy.imageHint: The compressed system image and RAM overlay are already included in total occupancy. They are not disposable file cache and are not added a second time.
editor.imageReferenceHint: Digest or Compose expression: edit the complete image reference above.
editor.imageInvalid: Enter an image reference with a valid tag (up to 128 characters: letters, numbers, _, . and -).
apps.imagesHint: Each service has its own tag. App store defaults are preserved; latest applies only without a tag or digest.
apps.correctFields: Please correct the highlighted fields in the form.
files.inspectTarget: Checking the destination and existing files …
files.driveReadOnly: Mounted read-only – files can be copied.

error.file_job_busy: The job is still running or saving its final status. Try again shortly.
files.scopeDeferred: Calculating the size is taking longer. When you start, the full size will be calculated and checked against free space before any files are copied.
api.title: API and CLI
api.cliHint: The titanosctl Go CLI uses the same permissions. See docs/PUBLIC-API.md in the repository.
api.security: Tokens belong to your account and can be revoked individually. Only hashes are stored. Last use is tracked in memory.
api.name: Name
api.scopeHint: Write permissions are off by default. A token can never exceed your account permissions.
api.once: Store it securely now. This token is shown only once.
api.revokeConfirm: Revoke “{name}” immediately? Applications using this token will lose access.
error.invalid_api_token: Invalid token name, permissions or token limit.
netx.migrationHint: Existing settings stay active until you explicitly test and confirm the new topology.
netx.intro: Named networks for management, storage and applications.
netx.confirmHint: Open the new management address and confirm there. Without confirmation the previous configuration is restored.
netx.unsaved: Network changes have not been applied
netx.bridgeEnabled: Bridge available for containers and VMs
netx.external: Router, DHCP and firewall remain external. Existing Docker and Tailscale rules are preserved.
netx.switchHint: LACP needs matching switch configuration. VLANs also need to be configured on the external switch and router.
netx.tailscaleHint: Tailscale routes, DNS and exit-node settings are preserved. Access rules remain managed in Tailscale.
netx.proxyHint: Public app URLs do not configure a tunnel. Tunnels and reverse proxies remain managed in their respective application.
netx.dnsHint: IPv64 and Cloudflare DNS update names and addresses. A DNS record creates neither a tunnel nor a port forward.
netx.name: Name
netx.bridge: Provide a bridge for VMs and containers
netx.addressHint: DHCP comes from the external network. Static addresses and Docker pools must be outside its DHCP range. Only the preferred management network automatically accepts default routes and DNS.
netx.removeConfirm: Remove “{name}” from the draft? Applying checks whether containers or VMs still use it.
lan.title: LAN networks
lan.intro: Containers with their own addresses on the external network.
lan.needParent: Set up and confirm a named NAS network first.
lan.driverHint: ipvlan L2 shares the parent MAC; macvlan uses individual MAC addresses.
lan.rangeHint: Exclude this pool from the external DHCP server and other static address assignments.
lan.hostAccess: Set up reachability between the NAS and containers
lan.hostHint: Unused address in the same subnet, outside the container pool and external DHCP range.
lan.external: Access rules come from the external router or switch. TitanOS does not configure its own firewall.
lan.removeHint: Remove LAN network “{name}”? Saved applications and connected containers must be moved to another network first.
lan.autoHint: Leave empty for Docker to allocate an address from the reserved pool. Static addresses must be inside the pool.
lan.privateHint: Private application networks and other services are preserved. Saving recreates the containers.
lan.assignError: This Compose network assignment cannot be edited safely. Use the Compose editor instead.
cleanup.title: Old plugin versions
cleanup.protectedHint: In use or required for rollback/update
cleanup.safety: Active, current, fallback and prepared update releases are protected. Sizes are estimates; shared blocks may reduce actual space freed.
media.title: Media imports
media.intro: Store ISO files and disk images on a data volume.
media.reselect: Select the original file to resume
media.originalFile: Select the original file with the same name and size. All previously uploaded bytes are checked before resuming.
media.background: Downloads and extraction continue on the NAS when this page closes. Browser uploads need the open page and can be resumed with the original file.
media.archiveHint: Supports gzip, xz and ZIP with exactly one supported image. Its type must match the output filename. The source and extracted image temporarily need space on the data volume; existing files are never overwritten.
media.removeHint: Remove job “{name}” and its temporary data? Published media are kept.
media.cancelHint: Cancel import “{name}” and discard temporary data?
media.virtioHint: The stable driver ISO comes from the official VirtIO-Win project and is assigned as a second CD drive.
media.virtioLoading: Downloading VirtIO drivers. The VM can be created when the download finishes.
error.media_busy: The media import is still active.
error.invalid_lan_network: The LAN network settings are invalid.
error.lan_exists: This LAN network is already configured.
error.lan_in_use: The LAN network is still in use or a network change is in progress.
ops.growEraseWarning: The new disk {disk} is erased and added to the RAID of {volume} as an additional member. All data on this disk is lost.
ops.resumeConfirm: The pending expansion of {volume} resumes from the displayed state. Keep the recovery volume connected; other storage changes stay blocked until it finishes.
ops.cancelGrowthConfirm: The expansion of {volume} that has not started is cancelled and its new spare is removed from the array if present. Data already erased on the new disk does not come back.
snapshot.deleteText: The snapshot “{name}” of {volume} is deleted for good. The current data on the volume stays.
assistant.destroyText: “{action}” changes or deletes “{name}” for good. This cannot be undone.
users.resetTwoFactorText: Two-factor login for {name} is turned off and the recovery codes stop working. All sessions of {name} end; after that the password alone signs in until 2FA is set up again.
ssh.removeText: Nobody can log in to your account over SSH with the key “{name}” afterwards.
ssh.removeLast: This is your last key. You will have no SSH access until you add a key again.
access.certRemoveText: Your certificate and its key are deleted from the NAS. The web UI then uses the self-signed certificate of TitanOS again; browsers will warn when you open it until you accept the exception.
files.trashEmptyAll: Empties the recycle bins of all {count} accounts in {share} completely, not just the open folder.
files.trashEmptyAccount: Empties the whole recycle bin of the account {account} in {share}, not just the open folder.
editor.jobLost: The apply job is no longer known (TitanOS may have restarted). Whether the change was applied is unknown – please check the state of the app.
power.workloadsNote: Running containers and VMs are shut down cleanly.
power.maintenanceNote: Running storage maintenance (rebuild, check) may be interrupted; mdadm resumes RAID maintenance by itself after the start.
power.diskTestNote: Running disk tests (prepare disks) do not survive a restart and have to be started again afterwards.
power.afterRebuild: Only after the running rebuild or check has finished
power.waitingRestart: The restart is scheduled and starts once rebuilds and checks have finished. Restarting titand drops it.
power.waitingShutdown: The shutdown is scheduled and starts once rebuilds and checks have finished. Restarting titand drops it.
power.pendingRestart: {user} scheduled a restart after the rebuild.
power.pendingShutdown: {user} scheduled a shutdown after the rebuild.
power.wakeOnLanNote: With Wake-on-LAN switched on (Settings › Energy), the NAS can also be switched on again over the network.
